latest_release.name: RGB MoCap Connect 0.5.0 - UE 5.7.4 Win64
latest_release.body:
RGB MoCap Connect now streams body motion to stock UE5 Manny and Quinn meshes as well as MetaHuman characters. In Unreal Editor, open **Tools > RGB MoCap Connect** and choose the target type when connecting each source. A supported Skeletal Mesh Actor or a Blueprint instance with a compatible mesh can receive motion.

- Assign different sources to Manny, Quinn, or MetaHuman actors in the same level.
- Mannequin body retargeting uses the selected mesh's bone lengths and updates the standard hand and foot IK bones. Face streaming is available on MetaHuman connections.
- The sender protocol is compatible with the 0.4.0 receiver.

Download the Win64 archive for **Unreal Engine 5.7.4**. Close the editor and extract the archive into your project's Plugins directory. When upgrading, replace the existing RGBMoCapMetaHuman plugin folder with the folder from the archive.

[Installation and streaming guide](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap/blob/main/docs/UNREAL_LIVE_LINK.md) · [Validation notes](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap/blob/main/unreal_plugin/RGBMoCapMetaHuman/VALIDATION.md#050-mannequin-and-mixed-targets)

# RGB MoCap

![RGB MoCap workspace showing video tracking and a 3D motion preview](docs/images/rgbmocap-workspace.png)

A native Windows app that turns video into editable human animation. Review and
export motion with AI processing running locally.

## Sample videos

### Motion capture

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b948dd8c-43b9-493a-9d7f-2fae0317695e

[Download original sample](docs/samples/motion-capture.mp4)

### Character retargeting

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1759f1bf-a0d0-409f-84d8-dde9409cfe6f

[Download original sample](docs/samples/character-retargeting.mp4)

### Multi Cam MoCap

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c0b290b-4a65-4287-8d22-c63c96b3d080

[Download original sample](docs/samples/multi-cam-mocap.mp4)

### Streaming to Blender

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc0e79bb-ecce-4752-ae14-3b6cea30c810

[Download original sample](docs/samples/streaming-to-blender.mp4)

### Unreal Engine MetaHuman live streaming

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3353f5ca-6393-40af-822f-210a77f51003

## Install and run

The steps below cover Windows. For the experimental x86-64 Linux AppImage and
source installation, see the [Linux guide](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap/blob/linux_support/docs/LINUX.md#test-the-appimage-on-linux-mint).
The AppImage was tested on WSL 2. Native Linux Mint testing is welcome.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> On Windows 11, Smart App Control in **On** mode may block the unsigned private
> Python runtime used by RGB MoCap. This can stop installation or launch.
> See [Smart App Control troubleshooting](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#smart-app-control-on-windows-11).

1. Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win). Use a short, writable
   installation path such as `C:\RGBMoCap`. Open **Command Prompt** to clone
   the repository. Adjust the path if you need a different folder.

   ```cmd
   git clone https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap.git C:\RGBMoCap
   cd /d C:\RGBMoCap
   ```

2. Prepare the runtimes for ExMR, FlowHMR and GVHMR with their supported add-ons,
   Blender, FFmpeg and native motion correction. AI weights and registered body
   files are downloaded separately in Model Manager:

   ```cmd
   install.cmd
   ```

3. Start the app:

   ```cmd
   RGBMoCap.cmd
   ```

   Keep the console open while the app runs. Prepare the AI model files separately
   using **Model Manager**; some require account registration and manual download.

If setup fails with `WinError 3` or `WinError 206` and the error shows a long
path, see [Windows path length troubleshooting](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#windows-path-length-during-installation).

To update, close the app and run `update.cmd` from the same folder. See the
[installation guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#install) for disk space, prerequisites
and recovery. If you used PEAR in RGB MoCap, see
[real-time tracking and existing installations](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#real-time-tracking).

Updates reuse recently verified, unchanged runtimes. If MAMMA camera-alignment
support preparation fails after the base installation succeeds, the base app
remains usable. Rerun `install.cmd` to retry the unavailable support. See
[verification and repair](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#installation-verification-and-repair).

### Optional model runtimes

`install.cmd` prepares ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR and camera alignment support
for MAMMA. Install the following only if
you use them, after the base installation:

| Model | Separate setup command | Installation and usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAMMA | `Setup_MAMMA.cmd` | [MAMMA guide](docs/MAMMA.md) |
| PromptHMR | `Setup_PromptHMR.cmd` | [PromptHMR guide](docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md) |
| GEM-X | `Setup_GEMX.cmd` | [GEM-X guide](docs/models/GEMX.md) |
| ViDiHand2 (experimental) | `Setup_ViDiHand2.cmd` (source only, reuses FlowHMR) | [ViDiHand2 setup and workflow](docs/FIRST_PERSON_ARMS.md#local-runtime-setup) |

MAMMA and PromptHMR require **Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools**, the Windows SDK and
**CUDA Toolkit 12.8** for local native builds. Close the app and review the
provider terms before setup. Then reopen it and prepare the selected model's
files in **Model Manager**. Their optional runtimes do not require each other;
`install.cmd` and `update.cmd` do not install them.

GEM-X uses the existing ExMR Python base with its own pinned inference packages.
Run its separate setup after `install.cmd`, then prepare its public files in
**Model Manager**. It does not require the C++ build tools or CUDA Toolkit.

For optional text-prompt and click-guided **Find person** tracking on Windows,
run `Setup_SAM31.cmd` after the base setup. Then choose **SAM 3.1** next to
**Find person** and use **Auto Download** on its 1.75 GB checkpoint row in
**Model Manager**. SAM 3.1 uses more VRAM than **Default** tracking.
**Resource Mode > Automatic** can offload tracking state and masks to system
RAM when VRAM is tight and retry once after CUDA runs out of memory.
See the [SAM 3.1 tracker guide](docs/models/SAM31.md#vram-use).

**Track Face** adds CPU face tracking for saved video. The 3D viewport shows
facial landmarks on SMPL-X, SMPL-H and SOMA surfaces. **Export Face** saves
ARKit-style coefficients alongside the chosen motion as TXT or Unreal Live Link Face CSV.
Face preview landmarks and Unreal-streamed expression coefficients use One Euro smoothing automatically. **Set Neutral** beside Track Face calibrates the selected person from the current frame, with saved per-person baselines and Reset. Saved face coefficients can also accompany Unreal Live Link body streaming; enable **Face** in the separately installed RGB MoCap Connect plugin. See [Face capture](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#face-capture) and [face streaming](docs/UNREAL_LIVE_LINK.md#optional-metahuman-face-streaming).

### Install with an AI agent

After cloning, open this repository folder in a local coding agent such as Codex.
The [agent guide](docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md) covers setup, models, capture, retargeting,
projects and resources. For example, ask:

```text
Help me install and run RGB MoCap on this Windows PC.
Read AGENTS.md and docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md first. Check the GPU and free disk space,
run install.cmd, and launch RGBMoCap.cmd. Help me prepare the ExMR model files.
Preserve existing models, projects and settings, and keep the pinned runtimes.
Tell me when I need to sign in, accept provider terms or download a file manually.
```

For multi-camera capture, add:

```text
Also enable MAMMA. Follow docs/MAMMA_AGENT_SETUP.md to check the C++/CUDA tools,
run Setup_MAMMA.cmd after the required license review, and verify the native CUDA
modules. Help me prepare its models without changing the other model runtimes.
```

For PromptHMR instead, add:

```text
Also enable PromptHMR. Follow docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md and docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md.
Check the C++/CUDA tools, run Setup_PromptHMR.cmd after the required license
review, verify its CUDA checks, and help prepare the exact Model Manager files.
Keep other runtimes and existing projects unchanged.
```

MAMMA's [agent setup guide](docs/MAMMA_AGENT_SETUP.md) and the
[PromptHMR guide](docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md) include build checks and recovery.
Provider login and license acceptance remain your responsibility;
do not put passwords or account tokens in the agent chat.

For scripted reconstruction, export and streaming, see the [command-line guide](docs/CLI.md).

## Features

- Optionally use RIFE frame interpolation for videos below 30 fps before offline
  reconstruction. The standard converter is the default. [RIFE setup and usage](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#rife-frame-interpolation)

- Manage model files across workflows in one window. See which workflows share each file, filter to dedicated models, and remove installed files after reviewing the affected workflows. [Model Manager guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#prepare-models)
- Reconstruct one or several people and preview the body mesh and animation bones.
- Reduce sliding with foot/palm contact correction and editable contact timings.
- Retarget motion to Mixamo FBX, VRM and PMX humanoid characters.
- Export source animation as FBX or BVH (Generic/Blender or 3ds Max Biped), with FBX A/T reference poses, an optional leading reference frame, per-person origin placement and symmetrical rest pose; export characters as FBX with or without meshes,
  or PMX character motion as VMD for MMD.
- Export portable Blender projects with source animation, video and saved cameras; MAMMA can include animated body meshes and every camera.
- Export animation for the stock UE5 Manny or Quinn skeleton. Include the bundled skinned mesh when the Unreal project has no mannequin assets. [UE5 mannequin FBX guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#ue5-mannequin-fbx)
- Export the current take, all takes for checked people, or individual takes. The export dialog shows what to do for each unavailable take. [Export guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#fbx-and-blender)
- Stream selected people's bones to Blender during playback or scrubbing, then bake their full recorded motion into Blender Actions. [Download the Blender add-on ZIP](blender_addon/rgbmocap_bone_stream.zip?raw=1) · [Installation and controls](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#stream-bones-to-blender)
- Stream motion to UE5 Manny and Quinn or to MetaHuman actors through Unreal Live Link. MetaHumans also support tracked expressions. [Prebuilt Windows bundles and installation](docs/UNREAL_LIVE_LINK.md#prebuilt-downloads) · [Controls and manual retargeting](docs/UNREAL_LIVE_LINK.md)
- Preview and correct GEM-X's native SOMA motion, retarget to humanoid characters, and export the Native77 skeleton as FBX or BVH. The Blender bundle includes the evaluated surface and input video.
- Save side-by-side input video and the current 3D viewport as MP4 with **File > Export Preview...** (offline models).
- Inspect source-video/bone alignment in Camera Preview and display saved cameras in 3D, with optional background rotation refinement for FlowHMR/ExMR.
- Capture hands and camera-driven head motion from first-person video with ViDiHand2. Preview MANO hands, optionally fit arms with IK, and export the first-person skeleton as FBX. [ViDiHand2 guide](docs/FIRST_PERSON_ARMS.md)
- Save projects with separate results for each AI model.
- Reduce FlowHMR memory use with query-batched attention and optional sparse hand sampling; optional HaMeR refines fingers. See [controls and trade-offs](docs/models/FLOWHMR.md#controls) and [measured time/memory comparisons](docs/PERFORMANCE.md#flowhmr-query-batches-and-four-frame-hands-2026-11-03).
- Reduce camera-estimation VRAM with default-on **VGGT-Ω OPT** in FlowHMR and automatic MAMMA calibration. It also works in Low Memory mode. [Measured camera VRAM](docs/PERFORMANCE.md#vggt-camera-memory-with-opt)
- For real-time webcam or video tracking, use [RGB MoCap Live](https://github.com/toyxyz/rgbmocap_live).

## How it works

1. Select an AI model and prepare its files in **Model Manager**, then use
   **File > Open Video**. For MAMMA, select it before opening synchronized camera
   videos; thumbnails switch the preview and one timeline trim applies to all views.
2. For ExMR, FlowHMR or GVHMR, optionally use **Find person** to select people.
   Choose **Default** or use [SAM 3.1](docs/models/SAM31.md#track-people) for
   text prompts and click selection.
   PromptHMR tracks people together during reconstruction.
   MAMMA detects people during reconstruction; keep **VGGT-Omega + GeoCalib (Automatic)** and
   enter an approximate **Reference Height (m)**, or import camera calibration.
   Click **Reconstruct 3D**.
3. Review the motion. For models with Motion Correction, edit contacts if needed
   and click **Apply Correction**.
4. Use **File > Export...** to choose a format supported by the source model, or
   import a character, retarget the motion and export it.

In Blender 5.0 or later, use the [Toyxyz Blender Retargeter](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz-blender-retargeter)
add-on to transfer exported RGB MoCap animation to another humanoid rig.

## Supported AI models

In our subjective tests, **PromptHMR** could improve relative placement and
interactions between multiple people in a **single video**, but its overall
motion quality was lower than **ExMR**. It does not support finger tracking.

| Model / original project | Body representation | Fingers | Setup and use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ExMR](https://github.com/twehrbein/ExMR) | SMPL-X | Included | [ExMR guide](docs/models/EXMR.md) |
| [FlowHMR](https://github.com/flowhmr/flowhmr) | SMPL-H | Included | [FlowHMR guide](docs/models/FLOWHMR.md) |
| [GVHMR](https://github.com/zju3dv/GVHMR) | SMPL-X | Optional HandFlow add-on | [GVHMR guide](docs/models/GVHMR.md) |
| [MAMMA](https://mamma.is.tue.mpg.de/) · multi-view motion capture | SMPL-X | Included | [MAMMA guide](docs/MAMMA.md) |
| [PromptHMR](https://github.com/yufu-wang/PromptHMR) | SMPL-X | Not generated | [PromptHMR guide](docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md) |
| [GEM-X](https://github.com/NVlabs/GEM-X) · fast processing, relatively low motion quality in our tests | SOMA Native77 | Included | [GEM-X guide](docs/models/GEMX.md) |
| [ViDiHand2](https://github.com/NTUYWANG103/ViDiHand) · first-person capture | Hands and camera-driven head, optional arms | Included | [ViDiHand2 guide](docs/FIRST_PERSON_ARMS.md) |

Requires 64-bit Windows, a compatible NVIDIA GPU/driver and OpenGL 4.3.
Model files are acquired separately; some require registration and license acceptance.

**Installed models and runtimes:** approximately **77.8 GB (72.5 GiB)** for the
six full-body workflows, including supported add-ons, Blender and FFmpeg, when the GEM-X CUDA files can be shared. Based on the measured inventory, excluding
projects, caches or retained downloads; shared files are counted once.
ViDiHand2 reuses the installed FlowHMR runtime. Its source and checkpoints
are outside this inventory.

| Configuration | Runtime | Models | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ExMR + FlowHMR + GVHMR and supported add-ons | 12.35 GiB | 28.89 GiB | 41.23 GiB |
| MAMMA additional files | 6.11 GiB | 3.53 GiB | 9.65 GiB |
| PromptHMR additional files, Fixed Camera | 6.22 GiB | 6.13 GiB | 12.34 GiB |
| GEM-X additional files, with CUDA sharing | 2.13 GiB | 7.11 GiB | 9.24 GiB |
| **Six full-body workflows** | **26.81 GiB** | **45.66 GiB** | **72.46 GiB** |

If GEM-X cannot share the verified CUDA DLLs, add about **2.95 GiB**.

Optional PromptHMR moving-camera support adds approximately **18.6 MiB** of
native modules and **1.55 GiB** of weights beyond these totals; see its model guide.

**MAMMA, PromptHMR and GEM-X require separate runtime installation.** Run
`Setup_MAMMA.cmd`, `Setup_PromptHMR.cmd` or `Setup_GEMX.cmd` after `install.cmd`, as described
[above](#optional-model-runtimes). They are not installed by `install.cmd` or
`update.cmd`; obtain weights separately in Model Manager.

App source, C++/CUDA compiler tools, installation temporary files and saved work
need additional space. These are measured sizes, not a setup free-space guarantee.
See [storage and installation details](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#installed-size).

[Cache and project cleanup: paths and deletion effects](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#storage-and-cleanup).

## Resources and speed

Start with **Resource Mode > Automatic**. It uses the fast supported path when
memory permits and falls back to a supported Low Memory path when needed.
Memory-saving methods depend on the model; **Low Memory** can trade slower
loading/transfers and more system RAM for lower VRAM use. See each model's guide
for implemented options and limits. **Resource Safety**, below Resource Mode,
defaults on. Turn it off to bypass low-RAM stopping and the VRAM allocator limit;
Automatic batching and actual allocation-error handling stay active. See the
[Resource Safety details](docs/PERFORMANCE.md#resource-safety).

Short paired tests reduced peak allocated VRAM from **5.68 to 3.87 GiB** for ExMR
and **6.10 to 2.77 GiB** for FlowHMR. Separate short-clip tests of connected
processing phases cut worker time by **44% for ExMR** and **24% for FlowHMR**,
with unchanged measured peak VRAM. These are different tests, not full-job
speed guarantees. See [resource modes, measured savings and acceleration](docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
for conditions, per-model results, direct-video preprocessing and output differences.

FlowHMR's **Adaptive Batching** selects 1–16 Fast SAM frames from available memory;
Low Memory uses one. Warm feature tests took 16–23% less time at batch 16 than at
batch 4, with peak allocated VRAM rising from 3.84 to 5.43 GiB. Whole-job gains can
be smaller. Batch selection and OOM retry messages appear in Console and CMD.
